Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh · Chandela, c. 1025–1050 CE (Krishna Deva)

Kandariya Mahadeva Temple: an evidence-tagged 3D reconstruction

Built at true scale from Alexander Cunningham's survey and plan. Every element and fact carries an evidence tag, and the sources are listed in the panel. Drag to orbit, right-drag or Shift-drag to pan, pinch to zoom (or click the model, then scroll). In walk mode, use WASD or the arrow keys, or the on-screen pad.

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Published 11 November 2026 · Updated 12 November 2026

The Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest standing temple at Khajuraho, built during the Chandela dynasty, who ruled the region in the 10th and 11th centuries CE. This model is built from the measurements Alexander Cunningham published from his 1864–65 survey and from his ground plan.

About this model

Cunningham describes the temple as having the usual portico, hall, great hall, vestibule and sanctum, "each of which has its separate pinnacled roof rising in regular gradation from the low pyramid of the entrance to the lofty spire of the sanctum". A second pair of transepts lights the passage round the sanctum, which is why he calls the plan a large double cross rather than a single one.

What the model does not show: the sculpture. Cunningham counted 872 statues on and in the temple, and no deity figures are modelled here. The sanctum holds a marble liṅga, drawn as a plain shape with a label.

All the key facts as text
LengthMeasured 33.2 m (109 ft) externally
WidthMeasured About 18.1 m (59½ ft) externally; Fergusson gives 60 ft (18.3 m)
HeightMeasured 35.5 m (116½ ft) above the ground; 26.8 m (88 ft) above its own floor
Floor levelMeasured 8.7 m (28½ ft) above the ground: the difference between the two heights
PlanDocumented Portico, hall (mandapa), great hall with transepts (maha-mandapa), vestibule (antarala) and sanctum (garbha-griha), with a passage round the sanctum lit by three open porticoes at the back and sides: a "double cross"
RoofsDocumented Each part has its own roof, rising in steps from the low pyramid over the entrance to the tall spire over the sanctum
SanctumDocumented A marble liṅga, shown here as a plain labelled shape
SculptureDocumented Cunningham counted 226 statues inside and 646 outside, 872 in all (not modelled)
DynastyDocumented Built during the Chandela dynasty, who ruled the region in the 10th and 11th centuries CE
Chamber sizes, wall and roof heightsEstimated Read from the published plan and photographs, not from a measured section
Smaller spires round the towerDocumented 84 smaller replicas of the main spire (Krishna Deva). Their grouping in the model is estimated
Terrace and base mouldingsEstimated How the 8.7 m rise divides between the shared terrace and the temple's own base
PersonIllustrative 1.7 m (5 ft 7 in), for scale

Sources

  1. A. Cunningham, Four Reports Made during the Years 1862-63-64-65, Archaeological Survey of India Reports vol. II (1871), pp. 419–420, and plate XCVII (plan).
  2. Krishna Deva, Khajuraho (Archaeological Survey of India, World Heritage Series), full text.
  3. D. N. Shukla, Vāstu-Śāstra (1960): the dimensions and the double-cross plan, quoted from an earlier survey.
  4. J. Fergusson, History of Indian and Eastern Architecture, revised edition (1910), fig. 342: plan of the Kandariya Mahadeva after Cunningham, 50 ft to 1 in.
  5. Archaeological Survey of India, World Heritage Sites: Khajuraho.
  6. UNESCO World Heritage List no. 240, Khajuraho Group of Monuments.
  7. Encyclopaedia Britannica, pradakshina (for the illustrative people walking round).
